config.title: Zustand for Global State

intro.title: Zustand for Global State
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that uses Zustand to manage a global state for a counter. You will learn how to create a Zustand store to hold and update shared data across components. The main technologies involved are Vue 3, Zustand (a state management library), and JavaScript. By the end, you'll understand how to set up a store, access state, and modify it from different parts of your app.
intro.usecase: Zustand's global state management is essential in Vue applications where multiple components need to share and react to the same data. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce dashboards where product filters, cart totals, and user preferences must stay synchronized across different UI sections. It's also crucial in collaborative tools like project management apps, where team members' status updates or document edits need to propagate instantly to all connected panels. Developers use Zustand to avoid prop drilling and maintain clean, predictable state flow in complex interfaces like admin consoles with live data visualizations and multi-step configuration wizards.

objectives: Initialize a Zustand store to manage global state in a Vue application
Construct reactive state slices and actions within a Zustand store
Integrate the Zustand store into Vue components using the useStore hook
Manipulate global state by dispatching actions from component event handlers
Bind component UI elements directly to reactive state from the store
Configure computed values (getters) derived from the global store state
Update multiple components to reflect synchronized changes from a single state source

steps.title: Import Vue and Zustand
steps.instruction: Import Vue and Zustand in the Vue component file. Use the import statement to bring in Vue from 'vue' and create from 'zustand'.
steps.hint: Remember to use the correct import syntax: import Vue from 'vue' and import { create } from 'zustand'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue component file now has the necessary imports for Vue and Zustand.
successCriteria: Vue is imported from 'vue' and create is imported from 'zustand'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue from 'vue' and create from 'zustand'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statements. You need to import Vue from 'vue' and create from 'zustand'.

steps.title: Create a Zustand store
steps.instruction: Create a Zustand store using the create function. Name it 'useCounterStore' and define it with an initial state containing a 'count' property set to 0.
steps.hint: Use the create function from Zustand to define your store. Inside, return an object with a 'count' property initialized to 0.
steps.seedCode:
import { create } from 'zustand';

// Create a Zustand store named useCounterStore with initial state { count: 0 }
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zustand store named useCounterStore is defined with an initial state object containing count: 0.
successCriteria: The store is created using create, named useCounterStore, and has an initial state with count set to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a store, but check that it's named 'useCounterStore' and has the initial state { count: 0 }.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use the create function and define the initial state properly.

steps.title: Define store state
steps.instruction: Inside the useCounterStore, define the initial state object with a property named 'count' set to 0.
steps.hint: Add an object with a 'count' property inside the store creation function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have an initial state object with count set to 0.
successCriteria: The useCounterStore function includes an object with a 'count' property initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an object with a 'count' property inside the store function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initial state object with 'count' property is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add store actions
steps.instruction: Inside the create callback, add an increment action function that uses set to update the count state by +1.
steps.hint: The set function receives the current state and returns the new state. For increment, you can use set((state) => ({ count: state.count + 1 })).
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have an increment action that increases the count when called.
successCriteria: The useCounterStore includes an increment function that uses set to update count by +1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an action, but check that it correctly uses set to update count by +1. The set function should receive a callback that returns the new state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment action is missing or incorrect. Add a function named increment that uses set((state) => ({ count: state.count + 1 })).

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named CounterDisplay using the Composition API setup function. The component should return a template with a single root <div> element.
steps.hint: Use the defineComponent function from Vue to create the component. The setup function should return an object with any data or methods you want to expose to the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CounterDisplay component is created with the Composition API setup function, ready to use the Zustand store.
successCriteria: CounterDisplay component is defined using defineComponent with a setup function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using defineComponent from Vue and have a setup function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to use defineComponent and include a setup function.

steps.title: Access store in component
steps.instruction: Inside the CounterDisplay component's setup function, access the Zustand store to get the current count value.
steps.hint: Use the useCounterStore hook you created earlier to access the store state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessing store state in a component
const count = useCounterStore((state) => state.count);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to the current count value from the Zustand store.
successCriteria: The CounterDisplay component's setup function accesses the count value from useCounterStore.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the useCounterStore hook to access the count value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't seem to be accessing the store state correctly. Try using useCounterStore to get the count value.

steps.title: Return store data to template
steps.instruction: In the CounterDisplay component's setup function, return an object that exposes the store's count state and increment action so they can be used in the template.
steps.hint: The return statement should provide the store data as properties that can be accessed in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns an object containing the store's count and increment, making them available in the template.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with count and increment properties from the store.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning both the count state and the increment action from the store.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function needs to return an object containing the store's count and increment. Check that you're accessing the store correctly and returning both values.

steps.title: Display store state
steps.instruction: Inside the CounterDisplay component's template, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value from the store.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output reactive data in Vue templates.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying reactive data in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterDisplay component will have a template that shows the current count value from the Zustand store.
successCriteria: The CounterDisplay component includes a paragraph element in its template that displays the count value using Vue's template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct template syntax to display the count value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The count value isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're using double curly braces {{ }} around the count variable in the template.

steps.title: Add buttons to trigger store actions
steps.instruction: In the CounterDisplay component's template, add two buttons: one with text 'Increment' that calls the increment action from the store, and another with text 'Reset' that calls a reset action (which you'll need to add to the store).
steps.hint: First add the reset action to the store (it should set count back to 0), then in the template add <button> elements with @click handlers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have both increment and reset actions, and the CounterDisplay component will have two buttons that can trigger these actions.
successCriteria: Store has increment and reset actions
CounterDisplay template has two buttons with @click handlers calling store actions
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure both the increment and reset actions are defined in the store, and both buttons have proper @click handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly connected to the store actions yet. Check that you've added both actions to the store and wired the buttons correctly.
